how_we_lost: WON on round 11 (digest T41). We stayed at 37-39 life with a small board through round 8 while P3's Angels, P2's Korvold/Mayhem Devil/Scute Swarm and P1's Teval fought each other. P3 killed Teval twice for us (Stroke of Midnight on T21, Generous Gift on T25). Muldrotha landed on round 7 (T26). On round 8 (T30) P1 was at 11 and tapped out: a 6-damage Muldrotha swing, then Syr Konrad from hand and Plaguecrafter recast from the graveyard (1 Konrad ping for leaving the yard, 4 death pings) killed P1 exactly. On round 9 (T33), Twisted Embrace on Konrad killed Serra's Emissary, Plaguecrafter went again, and an 11-power swing killed P2 from 13. Against P3: Hostage Taker took Vanquisher's Banner, Baba Lysaga drained 3, Vraska -3 hit Authority of the Consuls and then Giada, and recurring Plaguecrafter ate the blockers. On T41 Invasion of Innistrad killed the lone blocker (Valkyrie Harbinger) and a 16-power attack finished P3 from 9.
winnable_why: We won. The start was slow: a 2-land keep on 8 cards with no ramp put Muldrotha on round 7. But no opponent pressured us, and once the Konrad + Plaguecrafter + Muldrotha engine was online the strategist found lethal in each of the next four turns.
what_went_right: T10: Ratchet Bomb ticked to 1 destroyed BOTH opposing Sol Rings, and Plaguecrafter the same turn edicted Ramunap Excavator and Thraben Watcher. That slowed P2 and P3 early.
Low profile: we did not attack or threaten anyone until we could kill a player, so the table's combat went elsewhere (we took about 11 damage in 10 rounds).
T30: the executor correctly overruled Forge (which wanted Hostage Taker) to cast Syr Konrad, making Plaguecrafter's recast lethal on P1. The memo counted the pings exactly.

T33: the executor overruled Forge twice (Twisted Embrace on our own Konrad, then Plaguecrafter from the graveyard instead of Hostage Taker), and that killed P2. Correct kill order: always the lowest-life, tapped-out opponent.

T37-T41: we cleared the blockers each turn before combat (Vraska -3 on Authority and Giada, Plaguecrafter, Invasion at flash speed on Harbinger), and left Hostage Taker unsacrificed so Banner stayed exiled.

mistakes.what_happened: Round 6. The memo said: Nature's Lore, cast Soul-Guide Lantern as Braids fodder, keep Tropical Island + Underground Sea up for Counterspell, keep Vraska in hand. Vraska's -3 was named as the answer to Mayhem Devil. The executor instead accepted Forge's cast of Vraska, Golgari Queen, which tapped the Counterspell mana. It then OVERRULED Forge's -3 (which would have destroyed Mayhem Devil, MV3, or Insidious Roots) in favour of +2, sacrificing a Forest. Vraska was attacked to death over the next two opponent turns without ever using -3, and Teval resolved uncountered on T23.
mistakes.better_play: Follow the memo: Lantern plus Counterspell up. Or, if Vraska is cast, use -3 on Mayhem Devil right away.
mistakes.why: Mayhem Devil taxes every sacrifice this deck makes. It pinged us about 7 times in rounds 8-9 and turned our Baba/Braids/Plaguecrafter turns into damage for P2. A 4-mana walker traded for one card and one life.

mistakes.what_happened: At the end step there was no artifact on board, because Lantern had not been cast. Braids, Arisen Nightmare's trigger sacrificed Braids herself (Forge default, accepted). It drew 3 cards, which then forced us to discard Soul-Guide Lantern and Boseiju to hand size.
mistakes.better_play: Sacrifice Vraska. No opponent controlled a planeswalker, so all three had to lose 2 and we still draw 3, and the Braids engine stays on board. Sacrificing the fetched land or a tapped land would also have kept Braids.
mistakes.why: Braids was our only repeatable drain before Muldrotha. She was out of play from T22 until the graveyard recast on T37 (4 rounds).

mistakes.what_happened: Muldrotha resolved (entered tapped via Authority). But the land drop was Overgrown Tomb from hand rather than Marsh Flats from the graveyard, and nothing was cast from the graveyard. The memo's plan was Flats, fetch Swamp, cast Soul-Guide Lantern.
mistakes.better_play: Play the fetch from the graveyard (keep hand lands for later) and use the spare mana on a graveyard cast.
mistakes.why: It wasted the first Muldrotha turn's land lane and a mana. It was not costly here because nobody was attacking us.

mistakes.what_happened: Assassin's Trophy fired during our draw step. The executor overruled Forge's target (Gisela, the Broken Blade) and chose Zuran Orb. The memo said to hold Trophy through the opponents' turns for Hearthhull, Teval or Teval's Judgment. Hearthhull never appeared this game, and Teval resolved a round later with no answer in hand.
mistakes.better_play: Hold Trophy as the memo said, or at least spend it on an on-board threat.
mistakes.why: It was defensible, since the Hearthhull dossier says to kill Zuran Orb on sight. But Orb alone is a free land-sac outlet with no payoff on board. It cost nothing this game only because P3 killed Teval twice.

strategy_assessment: The plan was right for this table: stay small and uninteresting, use cheap edicts and Ratchet Bomb to slow the fastest starts, and let P3's Angels and P2's sacrifice deck fight P1. Then turn Muldrotha + Syr Konrad + recurring Plaguecrafter into burst damage aimed each turn at the lowest-life, tapped-out opponent. The memos' lethal arithmetic was accurate four turns in a row. Weak spots: the memos over-weighted Hearthhull (never cast this game) and held Counterspell for 40 turns without ever casting it. Mayhem Devil, the one card that punishes this deck, should have been the first removal target once it landed. The executor drifted off-plan on T22 (Vraska +2, Braids self-sacrifice), which cost about 4 rounds of Braids drain. Against a stronger table that drift could have mattered.
summary: A win built on low profile and burst: Ratchet Bomb killed two Sol Rings early, the table fought itself, and Muldrotha + Syr Konrad + recurring Plaguecrafter then killed P1 and P2 on consecutive turns before grinding out P3. The main process errors were on T22: Vraska +2 instead of -3 on Mayhem Devil, and Braids sacrificing herself instead of Vraska. Neither was punished here.
